review: 1:1–2 is the two-line opening stanza of the printed 88.88 – 88 shape, kept as two lines rather than padded to four, the same class as tr0218/0228. The rock-and-sand contrast is Matt 7:24–27 with Ps 62:3, and the Arabic صَخْرِي … رِمَال keeps both nouns, so the Hebrew keeps צוּר and חוֹל.

2:1–2 תִּקְוַת נַפְשִׁי … דַּם יֵשׁוּעַ וּשְׁמוֹ — the Arabic رَجَاءُ نَفْسِي وَحْدَهُ دَمُ يَسُوعَ وَاسْمُهُ is a verbless equation; the Hebrew keeps it verbless with אַךְ הִיא, because the stanza's point is that the hope *is* the blood and the name, not that it comes from them.

2:3 אֵין יְשׁוּעָה בִּלְעָדָיו — the Arabic لَيْسَ خَلَاصٌ بِسِوَاه is Acts 4:12 (וְאֵין בְּאַחֵר הַיְשׁוּעָה); the Hebrew keeps the noun יְשׁוּעָה and the negative, so the line is the apostolic claim and not a general statement about safety.

3:4 עֹגֶן נַפְשִׁי נָכוֹן — the Arabic مِرْسَاةُ نَفْسِي ثَابِتَه is 'my soul's anchor is firm'; עֹגֶן is post-biblical for anchor (the biblical verb is חָבַשׁ/עָגַן only in the sense of resting), accepted here because the Arabic's metaphor is nautical and Heb 6:19 supplies exactly that image in the Greek.

4:4 תִּשָּׁאֵר רִנָּתִי בִּשְׁמֵי — the Arabic يَبْقَى نَشِيدِي فِي سَمَاه is 'my song abides in His heaven'; רִנָּה is the jubilant cry (Ps 30:5, רִנָּה), kept rather than the flatter שִׁיר, because the stanza is about the song outlasting the singer.
